utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. Appearing for the Prosecution today, Mark Harmon, Barney Thomas, and Carmela Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are together in that. We are getting no interpretation. So I understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Perisic Defence today in the courtroom, Boris Zorko, Gregor Guy-Smith, and Novak Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And can I just welcome everybody back for the new year and wish that we can get on to the business of the case and finalise it as soon as possible. Counsel for the Defence, anything to tell us? Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hold on. I'm getting French interpretation now. Earlier I was getting nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I can hear the English. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. I can now hear the English, and just for the record, the Chamber is sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis today in the absence of Judge David. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that we move into private session for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Perisic has completed its case. There is a certain number of documents on the Defence side and on the Prosecution side that have not become exhibits yet due to technical reasons. What is most often the case is the fact that the translations are still pending or there are problems with regard to uploading the original documents. We filed a motion yesterday requesting the change of the status of certain documents. We have already been in touch with the CLSS, and we have received assurances the translations would be coming over the next few days. We have met with the Prosecution and discussed all of these technical matters related to our case. We also discussed some other topics, and perhaps Mr. Harmon would like to say a few words about what his intentions are now. However, as regards the MFI status of the documents that I mentioned a moment ago, I suggest that the Trial Chamber give us five days so that the parties sort this out together with the translators. I believe that by next Monday, we could sort out all the problems related to MFI documents and that we no longer encumber the Trial Chamber or the proceedings with all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Before I turn over to Mr. Harmon, should the Chamber understand that Mr. Perisic has completed his case to mean that the Defence rests?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The answer -- the answer to your question, Your Honour, is yes, with the exception, of course, to the extent there is some evidential matters that need to be attended to, some last-minute housekeeping matters. We need to have those -- those matters taken care of. But the Defence at this point rests inasmuch as there is no further testimony that the Defence intends to present to the Chamber at this time, and the only reason I'm saying that is in order to make sure that we preserve any rights with regard to the evidential issues that are outstanding concerning, as Mr. Lukic said, MFIs as well as translations. I hope that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's confusing even the more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't mean to be confusing at all. The Defence rests. The reason I am raising this is I don't want us to be in a position where we are foreclosed from dealing with some potential MFI issue or some translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: MFI issues are understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Obviously if they pass the test they will come in. If they don't they don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- but you're not calling -- you're resting. You are calling no further witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We are calling no further witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic, you referred to a motion that was filed yesterday with respect to the status of certain documents, I believe, and I would imagine with respect to that we'll have to await the response from the -- from the Prosecution and then it will take its course. Thank you so much. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have -- I agree with Mr. Lukic. We discussed yesterday the issue of the remaining and outstanding MFIs. If the parties have a week, we can resolve, I think, amongst ourselves those issues in large measure, if not in total. So we -- I agree with the Defence request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- of five days, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mentioned earlier in the course of the last month or two that we do have one rebuttal witness. That's -- will have to be an issue that we'll have to deal with a scheduling, because it's a delicate -- it's delicate getting this witness here. I will need some time. With sufficient lead time and a particular date, I can arrange that I'm quite confident. We have one additional matter which is in rebuttal but it will be in the form of a written motion that we'll file. It is to rebut a particular exhibit that was presented by the Defence. We will submit a written motion requesting that a document rebut or be admitted for purposes of your consideration in rebuttal of that document. So it's one witness and one motion that remains in our rebuttal case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: With respect to the scheduling of this witness, Mr. Harmon, is it not possible to also take advantage of these five days that the parties are asking for to sort out the MFI documents to be arranged in the scheduling of that witness so that we don't have to start making arrangements for scheduling only after some five days or after some two weeks. We have heard now that the Defence rests but for the MFI documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm perfectly amenable to that, Your Honour. I agree. I didn't mean to confuse or mislead the Court. I can start making those arrangements now. Just if I have a date when we're going to reconvene, then I can schedule him to come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the Court gave any impression that you were misleading, the Court is sincerely sorry for that. That was not the intention. The intention was just to say that for purposes of expeditiousness, can we just start all these things simultaneously so that those that take longer can slot in the shortest possible time after those that have come in earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome. Anything else that needs to be raised? Okay. If nothing else is there to be raised, then the Chamber will grant the parties five days during which to look at the MFI documents, and I hope that soon after that, those MFI documents will be placed before the Chamber to look at. We will be looking at the motions, and we will look at the rebuttal case of the Defence. It does seem as if we cannot postpone to a specific day unless you want to postpone to Monday next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think based upon the conversations we had with the Prosecution yesterday that that might be a bit premature just in terms of -- of the issue of scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Scheduling the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I don't know what Mr. Harmon has in mind. I think perhaps what we could do is we could inform -- perhaps inform the Court by next Monday of what our situation is and where we stand with regard to the potential rebuttal witness, but I don't know if that works for the Prosecution or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the five-day break that was requested was in relation, if I understood you well, with the MFI documents. I'm anticipating that by next week Monday or so, five days, to be -- for the Chamber to be seized of the MFI documents that the parties are talking about. The scheduling of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The rebuttal problem, Mr. Harmon indicated he needs some lead time. He's just going to take advantage of these five days but he might need more than that. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So but for anticipating any submissions by next week, we cannot schedule the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then the Court stands adjourned sine die. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: at 9.19 a.m., sine die.
